the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC observation: task-64d3df70 (unsolved)

Instance reached attempt cap (8 wrong submissions); 3 demo requests were provided. Preserve this for future recurrence. The grid is a mostly solid background with one small multicolor source motif and many singleton markers. Transformation is copying/stamping the source motif at each marker, replacing the marker with the value at the motif's anchor point; all unrelated background should remain unchanged. The main challenge is identifying the exact anchor point and bounding placement.

Verified demos:

1. Demo 1: background 5, source motif is 5x3 at rows 5-9, columns 6-8 (0-based):
`[[4,3,4],[5,3,2],[1,3,2],[2,6,8],[3,3,6]]`.
Output copies this motif at two target 0 markers, with background-color 5 cells visually unchanged. First copy occupies rows 6-10, cols 1-3; second rows 15-19, cols 2-4. First marker (r8,c1) becomes 1 and is the motif's row2,col0 cell. Second marker (r17,c3) becomes 3 and is motif row2,col1. Therefore marker-to-template alignment can vary; do not assume a universal central or unique-color anchor from this demo alone.

2. Demo 2: background 0; source row at bottom has motif `[8,6,8,6,8]` (with 0 padding). Every singleton 7 is replaced by a horizontal copy `[8,6,8,6,8]` centered on that marker: the marker cell itself maps to central value 8. Copy in bounds; preserve all other cells. This is a clear example of single-row motif with its center as anchor.

3. Demo 3: background 7; source horizontal motif `[1,4,6,6,9]` at row 8 cols 9-13. Every singleton 2 gets this horizontal motif centered on the marker; marker position maps to central value 6 (index 2). Copies may touch grid edges and are clipped to the grid. Preserve all other cells.

Test motif: vertical sequence in column 1, rows 1-5 (0-based), `[7,1,7,7,7]`, on background 9. Numerous singleton 8 markers. Likely stamp this vertical 5x1 motif at each 8, probably center-aligned (middle source cell=7 at relative row 0) based on demos 2-3; if so the per-marker offset sequence from top to bottom is `[7,1,7,7,7]`, with the marker location mapping to the middle 7. However all eight submissions were incorrect, so this inference is not verified and likely requires careful matching of exact source component/copy anchoring or a different placement rule. Do not reuse submitted grids as correct.

Attempt history: repeated attempts guessed inconsistent anchors/orientations and overlaid faulty vertical motifs. No accepted output. General durable lesson: identify the source motif’s exact cells and the target marker anchor by tracing every demonstration cell-by-cell; stamps use background-colored cells as transparent, and clipped placements may occur at edges. When anchor placement is ambiguous (as demo1 indicates), collect multiple examples and derive the rule before submitting.
